narrative.overview:
Congregation is the church's record books made legible. The public site is the visitors' book at the door; the admin dashboard is the registers themselves: the nominal roll, the attendance book, the collections ledger. Everything is built from the materials of a bound record book: white ledger pages laid on a cool rule-blue ground, feint blue rules between entries, a red double margin down the left of a page heading, a deep green bookcloth binding, blue-black ink, and small gilt stamps for dates and categories.

Density follows the audience. Public pages are generous and legible for first-time visitors and older congregants on phones: 16-18px body, 44-48px touch targets, 64-96px section rhythm, entries set as ruled rows with a big slab date in the margin. Admin pages are a working register: 14px body, ruled data tables with sticky headers, tabular figures in every column, white panels on the canvas ground, one bookcloth spine on the left. The admin follows the operating system into dark mode through CSS variables alone; the public site is always light.

The system rejects the church-template look (a stock photo hero over three icon cards) and the grey SaaS dashboard. Depth is quiet (hairline rules first, soft ink-tinted shadows second), corners are squared like a bound book, and colour is committed rather than decorative: bookcloth green is the one field colour, everything else is ink on paper.
keyCharacteristics: White ledger panels on a rule-blue canvas; feint blue hairlines as the default divider.
One structural signature: the red double margin, on headers and a single featured entry only.
Bookcloth green carries the nav band, footer, admin sidebar, and every primary action.
Bitter slab for headings and figures, Public Sans for everything read.
Tabular lining figures wherever a number appears.
Squared corners (6-8px), hairline borders, soft low shadows; no glows, no glass, no pills except avatars and status dots.
Admin follows OS dark mode via tokens alone; the public site never goes dark.

rules.name: The One Binding Rule
rules.body: Bookcloth green is the only colour that fills large areas. Every other hue appears as text, a hairline, a dot, or a soft tint.

rules.name: The Gilt Stamp Rule
rules.body: Gilt marks; it never carries. Use it for stamped meta (dates, categories, scripture references), column headings on bookcloth, and small marks like the crest and count chips. Never for body text, button fills, or button labels.

rules.name: The Margin Is Structure Rule
rules.body: Margin red exists only as the two hairlines of the double margin. It never colours text, icons, or fills; errors use `error`, live status uses `live`.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit in a column or be compared (counts, amounts, dates, times, page numbers, stat values, pagination summaries) is set with tabular lining figures. Tables get it by default; everything else takes the `num` utility. Money columns are right-aligned.

rules.name: The Slab Speaks, Sans Reads Rule
rules.body: Bitter is for headings, titles, and display figures. Anything a person reads in sentences is Public Sans.

rules.name: The Rows Before Cards Rule
rules.body: Lists of entries (events, service times, audit entries, messages, footer links) are ruled rows, not card grids. Cards are for items where a thumbnail carries meaning: sermons, gallery, leaders, roles.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: A border in `rule` defines the panel; the shadow only confirms it. Never a shadow without a border on a resting surface, never a coloured glow, never a hard offset shadow.

dos: Do use the semantic tokens (`surface`, `ink`, `rule`, `primary`) rather than raw palette colours, so admin dark mode follows automatically.
Do put the red double margin on page and section header blocks, the admin top-bar title, and the single featured hero entry panel.
Do set every count, amount, date, and time in tabular figures, and right-align money.
Do build entry lists as ruled rows with a Bitter date column before reaching for cards.
Do keep public body copy at 16px or larger with a measure under 70ch, and touch targets at 44px or more.
Do frame resting panels with a `rule` hairline and the resting shadow; save floating shadows for things that float.
Do use one icon family, Material Design Icons outline glyphs.
donts: Don't put the double margin on cards in a grid, list items, or table rows.
Don't set gilt on body text, button fills, or button labels; it is for stamps and small marks.
Don't place eyebrow or kicker labels above headings. Meta that carries real information (a date, a scripture reference) goes below the heading as a stamp.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, coloured glows, hard offset shadows, or a coloured left border wider than 1px on cards (toast status stripes are the single exception).
Don't use pill-shaped buttons or radii above 10px on surfaces; only avatars, dots, and round icon buttons are fully round.
Don't use emoji as icons, or fonts other than Bitter and Public Sans.
Don't let the public site go dark; dark tokens and the `dark:` variant belong to the admin shell only.
